answer: Treat each agent identity like a tree in a shared orchard: to plant one, the agent must lock a refundable bond in a public registry that acts as a beacon, so anyone can see how many identities one operator controls. The bond grows with each additional identity and stays time-locked; if two identities submit identical work or vote together, both bonds are slashed. A lone honest agent pays little, but a sybil farmer must fund every fake like a separate sonnet in a costly anthology, so the attack's price rises faster than its influence.
